title: One-on-One with Jason Licht: The Standard Remains | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: So, I know that in football there are no two offseasons are the same. It's always incredible that no roster is ever exactly the same year to year. So, each offseason's got to be a little unique. What about this one presented some unique opportunities or challenges for you? You're right that they are all different. It's a different puzzle every year that you got to put together. We we feel like we're still the same team that started off the year 6 and 2, 5 and 1 really. Um 6 and 2 with the bye week. It was a great bye week. Um but we just, you know, had some unfortunate injuries. Uh you know, a lot of things led to it. We never want to use that as an excuse, but we still have some very good players on our team. And you know, we have a start with the offense with our offensive line being one of the top ones in the league when we're healthy. And the receiver room that we have. Um Bucky, you know, Baker obviously. That if we can accentuate that offense, which I think will be one of the top offenses, has a chance to be even a little bit more. Um and make what's really good even better. Um I think that gives us a very good chance to having some success this year. But, yet at the same time this year, we have a lot of pieces on defense that we need to um also accentuate and and upgrade or get some more players. We have a lot of good players on that side of the ball. A lot of a lot of young players stepped up last year. Um some need to step up a little bit more this year and we're confident that they will. But, we had an opportunity to go out and find and look for what the best players that were there that fit into what we were doing, fit into the cap, fit into the puzzle there. But, it it was regardless of position. We really had a chance to just kind of focus on what the best player was. As you talk about defense and upgrading a few positions, I know of course Lavonte retiring huge impact on not just the defense, but this organization overall. What has he taught you about being a GM? How has he influenced you and and influenced the organization as a whole? We could sit here forever and talk about Lavonte. Uh jeez. He's such a presence just in his own way. Just the way he goes about business. I told him when I talked to him yesterday that uh you know, it's just been an honor to not just be around him the player because he's I think he's Hall of Fame going to be in the Hall of Fame at some point. Um but, just being around greatness was awesome. But, it was even more of a of a of a great thing to be around him the person. And I even told him I said I I want my kids to grow up to be like you. And it's, you know, to be the person that you are. Just selfless, just goes to work every day. Uh has a great attitude all the time. Makes everybody around him better. Um those are the kind of things that he brought to our organization and brought to me. He was a he was an ear I could I could rely on. Um I talked to him you know, probably more than or deeper than I would other players just because of the fact that he's been around so long and knows so much. And then of course, you're now having to say goodbye to your first ever draft pick that I know holds a special place in your heart. What is that like for you personally and then also for you as a GM? Yeah, that that one just, not going to lie, it was tough. In the same ways that I talked about Lavonte, you could echo it with Mike. Best player we've ever had on offense in franchise history. Just a unbelievable person on and off the field. He's uh I'm kind of going through the some of the stages of grief. Um kind of have have settled right now on acceptance. it was, you know, it was tough, but we had some great conversations. He's loves this team. Thinks that we're going to be a good team. Thinks we're going to be a great team. Loves his his room. Loves those receivers. Loves his quarterback. But, he was really it was almost like he was thinking of his partners there at the receiver room and giving them an opportunity now to be able to step up, which I know they can. And and have success themselves. Yeah, and and tell us about how you feel about that room that we know that Mike Evans is one of one. But, man to think about this wide receiver room that he has left behind. How do you see them stepping up? Who are the individuals that you see trying to fill the Mike Evans shoes if it were? Well, Chris always steps up. Chris is his his own entity. And Chris will now get more opportunities as well. But, Chris is going to be Chris. Which is really good. Um in his role. But, it's going to probably affect J Mac um [snorts] and Mecca a little bit more. And those two have you know, the ability to to just really thrive and become not just good young players, but to become names in this league. And then I can't forget about Tez. Um Tez in in the role that he's going they're going to carve out for him. Which will expand. Is going to be exciting. And then when it comes to adding new players, tell me about your philosophy as a general manager when it comes to free agency and trades in particular. And how does that philosophy get influenced by the particular maybe positions of need and what that looks like trying to add positions in free agency or trades? Well, they've got to be a good fit for what we're doing. Um they've got to be a good fit for our team. We've talked at length here about, you know, the type of character we look in players. But, that is also very important. But, you know, I do want to stress that that doesn't mean that we aren't going to invite some nasty mean aggressive uh whatever word you want to throw in there. That all is part of being a good teammate. Uh challenging others. Bringing a lot of energy. it's I think the guys that we that we signed this year especially on the defense, kind of epitomize that. So, we're excited about that. Yeah, let's let's talk about a few of those guys particularly on the defensive side. So, Alex Anzalone, Alkadeen Muhammad, A Shawn Robinson. And then of course, if you want to include special teams ace Miles Killebrew in as a defensive player. But, uh what do you see about the things of those individual guys that excite you and what they could bring to the defense individually and then all of them collectively? Alex has been a player that we've we've faced the Lions it seems like 100 times in the last 3 years. He's always in then of obviously when he was with the Saints. He's he's always been a little bit of a thorn in our side because of the fact that he's a really good Well, he's a he's a tough player. He's sideline to sideline. You know, he's got all that. But, he's a he's a really good cover linebacker, which is very very important in this league since we're playing against nickel most more majority of the time. And you know, it's been some areas that we've struggled in the past. And he brings that element, which which is really uh going to be uh it's going to be cool to see. Uh it's good for us. It's a good asset for us. Um A Shawn he's I just remember you know, the times that we've faced him. Especially going against him when he was in Carolina. Uh our offensive line That guy's a to block. You know, he is he's tough. He's strong. He's a big big body. He keeps coming. He's a really good run defender. Um and keeps after it and gives 100%. And Miles Killebrew has been one of the top special teams players in this league for a while. And Danny Smith has been you know, knocking down my door since he first got here uh talking about what kind of attitude and what kind of energy he brings as a captain of a special teams unit. And how much passion he puts into his role, which then bleeds into others. And that's something I'm really looking forward to. Yeah, knowing special teams is a unit that you guys wanted to be able to see improvement in this year. Looking at the addition of Killebrew and Danny Smith and then even re-signing Co. What of those moves do you feel like really inspires you and and thinks about, man this is this is going to make a difference for our special teams unit? We'll start with Danny Smith, one of the better special teams coaches the league has seen. Having him and his energy is has been has been awesome. And we already talked about Miles and Co. being a we call middleweight special teams player. You know, he he brings it every play. And he was somebody that jumped off the tape right away for Coach Smith. And then um uh Kenny Gainwell has also been uh a very good returner, but also a special teams cover guy that really has a you know, takes a lot of pride in doing that. And that's one thing that Danny Smith brings out in players. They he gets them excited, which can be sometimes a mundane role for some. But, when he's coaching, they seem to have a lot of excitement and pride in their job. Which leads me to think that our special teams are going to going to be very very good this year with all those additions. I like that. And you brought up Kenny Gainwell. Uh he and then Jake Browning are your your offensive new additions to the team. Uh tell me about what made you bring each of those guys in and and the thing you're excited about. Well, with Kenny, he's very good third down player. He's very good uh runner as well. Um he's takes a lot of pride in his blocking, but he's a excellent receiver. And the fact that he was the number two really in in Pittsburgh or at least started off the season and they went kind of one A one B that he was their MVP. It's you know, that that says a lot about a player and for us to be able to get him and what he's going to add to the dimension to our offense. He's got a lot of Bucky type movement. Um, it's very similar. I'm not saying that he's replacing Bucky by any means, but it's you know, it's a good thing to have along with Sean Tucker as a bigger back that can power through arm tackles and and pick up short yards um with a lot of speed too. So we've got you know, a three-headed monster right there right now hopefully and and uh we're really really happy. That was something that we were targeting the entire time. And then with um Jake, you know, he's played a lot of football for a backup um because of injuries there in Cincinnati. Thought it was a little bit, you know, last year they had a lot of injuries as well. Wasn't quite ideal situation for him. I think he's a lot better than some of the tape that he put on or some of the play that he put on tape last year, but kind of took a look at his body of work and you know, he's he's the type of person that fits that mold of a backup quarterback because what he can bring for Baker in that room um with his you know, the leadership and then also the experience that he's had. And then I know not only did you resign Cove, but also brought back Cade Otton. Um, I think he's a guy that sometimes is a little bit unsung for what he provides. I mean goodness, even just the number of snaps that guy can play is crazy. So what really made you guys want to bring him back and and what are the things he does for the offense that we don't always appreciate? Well, first of all, he's he goes about it the right way. He's selfless. He works his butt off. And what makes Cade so valuable is that you know, when you have a tight end you you you have some that are just receivers that F's we call them, some that are just blockers that are Y's. Um, and if you can find a Y which he is, we consider that also can receive and also block maybe not at a elite level at anything, but a really good level at everything. It makes that player a very very valuable player. So especially at that position. Now of course most importantly, we had an amazing source on the Cove news. That would be you. I love when you break your own news according to a source, of course. Uh, tell me what inspired you to first start doing this years ago and what are some of your favorite responses you get from people when you do this? Well, we always have a started about three years ago. We that last Friday of the first week of free agency kind of slows down and then you pick things back up on Monday. And with you know, some of the some of the second third wave type players um the following week, but when we have players that we know we're going to resign, um we've already kind of figured out what the market is. We've kind of come close to deals with their agents. They're just they're just waiting for us to call and and kind of finish it. Um we pick a player or two while we're out on a boat. So I have the whole crew Greenberg, Jackie, Rob McCartney, Mike Biel, Shane Skannel, Tony Hardy. I mean we'll have to add to that. Maybe get a bigger boat next year, but um we always end up as we're coming back in. We go out for two or three hours. As we're coming back into dock, we we finish it up with doing a signing and and and Cove just seems like a perfect boat guy. Who else are you going to sign on a boat? Yeah, well We did Ben Bredeson on a boat couple years ago on his first contract. So he's also a boat guy. A boat guy. This like now it's his own category of signees where you a boat guy. It's like it it feels like a special honor. >> Yeah, sure is. Absolutely. >> [laughter] >> That's great. I love it. And and now I know also as we talk about some of these offensive guys you've resigned or or new guys that you've signed, you also of course now have Zac Robinson as an offensive coordinator. What do you feel like he is going to do to help bring out the best in the guys that you've been able to put on this roster? He comes from a great mentor in Sean McVay. And sometimes that gets overhyped a little bit. Not nothing taking nothing away from Sean McVay. He's a great coach. But just because you work for somebody doesn't necessarily mean you're going to do it. But he he has proven um in Atlanta that especially when we played against them that he can get very creative. He doesn't just bring his offense. He he he he can modify it depending on what you have. And so when we first were going through the interview process, Todd and I with him, um he had studied our film. He knew our players. Um he gave us a big a plan of what he could do um with each and every single one of them. Um had a plan for Te'o, had a plan for Jay Mac, had a plan for Cade if we were able to bring him back. Had a plan in case Mike left. Um and it was just a it was very detailed and it just I think it just brings out some confidence in players. I know Baker was as very very excited um with his short um amount of time that he had with him um in LA. I think he felt that Zac was very responsible for getting him up to speed quickly in that two-day period before he or one-day period, whatever it was before he had to play and win that game for him. So I know that there's a lot of confidence. And then I know that for you we talked about, you know, free agency, trades, but the draft, that's your baby. That's where you love to build a roster. Why is the draft so important to your strategy of how you want to build the team? It becomes very important when you have a roster with now our players earn every penny that they're making, but we have some players making you know, at the higher end of the salary scale. And you know, when you get to that point, it limits you a little bit in what you can do in free agency. You have to look ahead. You have to look at the future. You have to look at you want to be able to resign your really good players and when their contracts are up, if you don't do it beforehand. So you need an influx of young players that are going to be able to have to contribute so you can keep the balance of the team. So I'm not saying we're moving on from planning on moving on from anybody, but at all. It's it's just when you have a a quarterback uh on a you know, second third contract, when you've got some you know, other players and I'm not saying they're limiting what we can do at all. We're very happy that we have them. But you need to bring in young players that can help. So um we've had a lot of success lately with the draft. We're signing a lot of our own players, which is why we're in that position and that's the goal. So you want to keep drafting well. That's the secret to uh having sustained success. Now I always love everybody talks about the draft and oh, taking the best player available, but we also know that need does factor in and you want to be able to take the best player available that also satisfies one of your needs. When you look at this year's draft, it feels like in certain years there's been themes for you guys of especially things like speed or special teams or whatever it may be. Are there themes this year for what you guys want to accomplish in the draft and then how well does this draft match that? This draft matches with what our needs are very well. Now that doesn't mean you're going to be assured to get one of those players. It's uh it can be a little bit a daunting task. You never know when your players that you like are going to be taken, but it does match up well. But you can never you can never go wrong if you have to veer course um and take another position that public or you know, the critics don't feel you need. At some point you're going to be happy you got that player. Uh showed up last year when we took Imecca. So I don't think anybody had that on their bingo card and it it really we're in a good position right now because of it. You know more about this team than pretty much anybody else. I don't know. And you care more about this team than pretty much anybody else in your role. I wouldn't say that. Tell me as you look forward to this season, what excites you? What do you find yourself just ready for it to be week one? What are those things that come to mind for you about this team? This team is really hungry right now and the way it ended last year, I think really lit a fire under a lot of players. Um I've had several of them telling me that they can't wait until OTA's start to get out there. And had several of them after the season ended last year texting or calling or whatever saying this is not going to happen next year. Um I just think I'm excited to see the the energy and just the uh just the way they're going to go about it and attack it this year. Perfect.
